messages.author: c4ad98ee09d9ee51
messages.subject: Discrepant result between point and line graph with same data
parts:
Hey everyone,

I'm trying to make a line graph that plots two different sets of data.
The problem I'm having is that much of the data isn't being included
in the graph and what does show up is a mix between the two data sets.
When I do the same thing, only changing geom_line to geom_point, all
the data is graphed. I need it to be a line graph where the two lines
are represented differently, which I haven't included yet. My code is:


DF <- read.table("LightCurve.csv", header=TRUE, sep=",")

MMO <- DF$MMO.645
AKO <- DF$AKO.645
JD <- DF$X

Mag <- c(MMO,AKO)

G <- ggplot(data = DF, aes(x = JD, y = -Mag)) +
geom_line() +
scale_y_continuous("Magnitude Difference") +
scale_x_continuous("JD - 2450000") +
coord_cartesian()

messages.subject: Re: Discrepant result between point and line graph with same data
parts:
Alexa,

This problem is being caused by the presence of NAs in your dataset. To make the data easier to work with, I melted it (see the reshape package) and used the na.rm argument to remove the NAs (see ?melt):

data <- read.table("C:\\Users\\Jonathan\\Desktop\\temp.txt")

library(reshape)
library(ggplot2)

new.data<-melt(data,id.var="X",na.rm=TRUE)

ggplot(new.data,aes(x=X,y=value,color=variable))+geom_line()

Jonathan
